title: Spamhaus analyses hosting providers behind phishing and fraud domains shared at Maple Disruption 2.0
place: Canada (Maple Disruption 2.0, Canadian law enforcement sprint)
geo_basis: Report is about phishing and fraud targeting Canadians; pin is a placeholder for Canada (Ottawa)
summary: Spamhaus published an analysis of the hosting providers and nameservers behind phishing and fraud domains shared at Maple Disruption 2.0, a sprint organised by Canadian law enforcement. Spamhaus says Cloudflare's abuse posture has not meaningfully improved, calls fxmail.club a likely rogue provider that it added to ASN-DROP, and says cloudzy.com is on ASN-DROP. It found no systematic avoidance of DROP or ASN-DROP networks by Canada-targeting actors.
plain: Spamhaus looked at which hosting companies carry phishing and fraud sites aimed at Canadians and says some are weak on abuse; it lists two on its ASN-DROP blocklist.
exec: Spamhaus's own analysis names hosting and DNS providers behind phishing aimed at Canadians; blocklist data may affect mail and web filtering.
action: Spamhaus advises applying BCL, DROP and ASN-DROP on perimeter devices such as firewalls and web proxies, and DBL on web proxies and DNS resolvers.

sources.name: Spamhaus: Maple Disruption 2.0 aftermath: Hosting providers enabling phishing and fraud targeting Canadians

validation.note: Only Spamhaus's own post read; findings are Spamhaus's own analysis and are stated as such.
